head_commit.message:
fix(pipeline): catch per-section language drift, drop empty sections, and keep the regenerate language (#1003)

* fix(pipeline): catch per-section language drift, drop empty sections, keep the regenerate language

Three owner-reported defects, all downstream of one architectural change: PRs
#969 and #992 moved generation from ONE whole-document call to per-section
calls that cannot see their siblings. Before that, coherence was free.

Language drift. content.language_mismatch read the whole document, and
languages_align returns the DOMINANT language, so a majority vote hid exactly
the reported case. Measured: one Italian section in a long English resume went
undetected, two undetected, three detected. A per-section pass now runs when
the document-level read comes back clean.

It is scoped POSITIVELY to Summary/Experience/Projects rather than by excluding
Skills. Review caught why that matters: SectionKind has six variants and
classify_section has no heading list for Certifications, Awards, Publications
or Languages-spoken, so all of them land in Other. A correct English "AWS
Certified Solutions Architect (Professional, 2022)" block clears the character
floor and reads as non-English - an exclusion list silently admits every kind
nobody thought of. A false Critical here blanks keywordCoverage and suppresses
every alignment finding on the whole document, so the cost of over-reach is
higher than the miss.

Empty sections. My own #998 regression: "order the sections EXACTLY as … do
not drop" read as a manifest plus a ban on omitting anything, so the model
emitted Projects and Publications with nothing in them. The prompt now frames
the list as an order, not a checklist.

The guard is a Warning, not a Critical, and the severity is the design. repair
acts on Criticals and its remedy is to REGENERATE the section - asked to fill
an empty PROJECTS the model would invent projects, a fabrication in the one
part of this pipeline built to prevent them. Removal is the right remedy and
model::adapter::push_nonempty_section already does it structurally, so nothing
empty reaches the rendered document.

Regenerate language. useTailorPipeline re-detected from jobDesc every render
and treated "I could not tell" as "it is English", discarding a language the
run already knew. It now prefers the persisted value - normalized through
toLanguageCode first, because extractMetadata persists a display NAME
("German") while every other writer stores an ISO code and save_application
merges both into one record. Passing "German" through would have been worse
than the bug: normalize_language truncates it to "ge", which matches no
languages_align arm, turning the language checks off entirely for that
document.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): make the splice boundary and the accept rule survive per-section generation

An audit measured what #969/#992 broke when generation moved from one
whole-document call to per-section calls that cannot see their siblings. Five
findings, one root cause each side of the same seam: the splice trusted the
model's reply, and the accept rule could not see the damage.

A repair round could silently delete a job. company_survives lowercased the
ENTIRE generated document and substring-searched for the employer, so a
Summary reading "…at Acme Payments and Globex Logistics" spared the deletion
of the whole Globex entry from EXPERIENCE. Measured: roles 2 to 1,
factual.dropped_role never fired, round accepted and persisted. Survival is now
tested against the generated EXPERIENCE section, all of its lines, so an
ordinary bullet reword still matches.

A reply containing the whole document was accepted and spliced over one
section. is_usable_replacement checked for a fence tag, a leading heading and
one body line, and nothing about how many sections came back. Measured: 6
sections to 10, and because reorder_sections is a stable sort, linearize merely
parked the duplicates adjacent - the exported PDF showed four sections twice.
Under mutation it compounded to 4x as the loop re-accepted round after round.

A reply for a DIFFERENT section was accepted. The target was resolved by
SectionKey and the reply spliced without re-classifying it, so asking for
SUMMARY and receiving SKILLS silently destroyed the summary and created a
second skills section, which the next round then could not find. The reply's
own heading is now re-classified and a mismatch is discarded - the right remedy
for a bad attempt is to drop it, not to raise a Critical that would ask the
model to regenerate again.

Analysis::section_of_kind returned only the FIRST section of a kind, so an
invented link in a second Projects section produced zero Criticals. The
Critical-severity consumer now reads every matching section; the two
Warning-severity consumers keep the cheaper lookup, since the residual risk
there costs a missed Warning rather than a missed Critical.

round_is_worse could only see Criticals and absences, while its sibling
humanize_is_worse also guarded coverage and voice - and repair runs FIRST,
makes up to eight blind per-section rewrites, and had the weaker rule. It now
reverts on a drop in roles_output, the one metric that saw the deleted job, and
shares humanize's coverage guard rather than duplicating it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(pipeline): let a section rewrite see the document it belongs to

Before #969/#992 a resume was generated by ONE model call, so language, voice
and tense coherence came free. The staged pipeline broke generation into
per-section calls that cannot see their siblings and replaced that implicit
guarantee with a prompt instruction - and instructions drift. Three
user-visible bugs followed, including a resume whose summary was English, work
experience Italian, and skills English again.

repair_user passed the source resume, the one section being rewritten, its
issues and an optional note. Nothing told the model what the rest of the
document looked like. It now also receives a compact anchor: the Summary,
which carries the register, and one representative Experience bullet, which
carries tense and voice - each excluded by SectionKind when it IS the section
being rewritten, so a rewrite never matches the text it is replacing.

An anchor rather than the whole document because this is charged up to
MAX_SECTIONS_PER_ROUND x max_repair_attempts = 8 times per run. Capped at
SIBLING_CONTEXT_CAP, roughly twice the measured worst case in this crate's own
fixtures and far below the whole-document cap humanize uses for its single
pass. The trade: drift confined to Skills or Education against the anchor is
not prevented, only detected.

This is model-generated text re-entering a prompt, so ADR-010 applies exactly
as it does to a scraped job ad. document_context is registered in
FENCE_TAG_PATTERNS and covered by the existing load-bearing forgery loop;
removing the registration lets a forged closing tag leak through, which the
test now proves.

The user's own regenerate-this-section button inherits all of it, since
resume_pipeline_regenerate_section calls the same function.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(pipeline): revert a repair round that introduces cross-section incoherence

An audit found the codebase's only two cross-section coherence checks -
duplicate.bullet and consistency.skill_not_demonstrated - are computed and then
thrown away. repair acts on Criticals only, humanize on voice.* only. Measured
consequences, both accepted and persisted: a round that doubled the whole
document produced 5 duplicate.bullet warnings at duplicateRatio 1.00 and
shipped; a round that deleted an employment entry produced 4
skill_not_demonstrated warnings and shipped.

The naive fix is to revert when those warnings are present, and it is wrong.
The same audit measured them false-positiving under per-section generation:
rewording two Experience bullets to drop the exact tokens - the ordinary
outcome of a rewrite that cannot see the Skills section - raises four warnings
on a truthful document. An absolute threshold would revert good rounds and
would need calibrating against noise.

So the term is a DELTA, not a count. The question is not whether the document
carries cross-section warnings but whether THIS ROUND introduced any that were
not there before. Four before and four after reverts nothing; four before and
nine after reverts. That needs no threshold, is immune to the measured baseline
false positives, and matches the before/after shape round_is_worse already uses
for its newly-introduced-absence term.

Per code rather than summed, so a round that fixes two duplicate.bullet
warnings while introducing two skill_not_demonstrated ones cannot hide a
regression behind an unrelated improvement - a case a summed total reads as
flat, and which the mutation check confirmed only the per-code form catches.

Also closes two advisories from the security review of da4926f0: the anchor is
trimmed once at its source, so repair_system's gate and repair_user's own
emptiness test can no longer disagree about whether a document_context block
exists; and the context rule now says to match the language and tense OBSERVED
there, naming it a writing sample rather than asking the model to conform to
untrusted content.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(validate): do not read an unrecognised experience heading as deleted jobs

Security review found a HIGH regression introduced by this branch's own
scoping of the dropped-role survival search.

company_survives used to read the whole generated document, which let a
Summary sentence naming a former employer mask the deletion of that employer's
entire entry. Scoping the search to SectionKind::Experience closed that, but
turned a second fact into the same verdict: when the generated resume has NO
Experience-kind section, the scoped haystack is empty, so every source role
reads as deleted.

classify_section knows work experience, berufserfahrung, employment and a few
more - it does not know Work History or Selected Roles, which land in Other.
Measured on a resume carrying both roles verbatim: heading WORK EXPERIENCE
gives 0 issues, WORK HISTORY gives 2 factual.dropped_role Criticals, SELECTED
ROLES the same. Those are terminal, not merely wrong: criticals_by_section
routes them to SectionKey::Experience, find cannot locate it, no repair runs,
and the run parks at needsReview telling the user two jobs vanished from a
document that still lists them.

Reachability rose in this same branch, which is what makes it urgent rather
than theoretical: draft_system was loosened from "do not reorder, drop, or
invent" to "an ORDER, not a checklist" so the model is freer to choose its own
heading, and matches_requested_kind constrains only a repair reply, never the
draft.

Absent is not deleted. The search now falls back to the whole document when no
Experience-kind section exists, mirroring the guard project_link_issues
already had - preferring a possible miss over a guaranteed false Critical,
since the scoping exists to catch a rare regression and must not manufacture a
common one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): resolve the blocking findings from the pre-merge review ensemble

Three reviewer passes plus a security gate, run over the whole branch. Every
finding below was reproduced before being fixed.

The Rust suite was RED and I reported it green. cargo test --lib and
--test architecture do not build tests/eval.rs; CI's nextest --all-features
does. The corpus guard was doing exactly its job - the new Italian-drift
fixture was graded by nothing - and the command I ran was narrow enough to
miss it. The fixture is now registered in CASES.

generated_experience_lower fell back on TEXT emptiness rather than section
absence. A wiped Experience section still yields one blank line, so the joined
text is empty, the fallback fires, and an employer named in the Summary masks
the loss. Measured: a resume with its entire employment history deleted
reported factual.dropped_role = 0 and ok = true. It now tests section
existence, mirroring project_link_issues' own presence guard.

section_language_issues gated on a SectionKind allowlist, a proxy for "is this
prose" that was wrong in both directions - too narrow to see an Experience
section headed Work History, too wide for a keyword-shaped one that whatlang
misreads. Replaced with a prose-density test: the share of words opening
lowercase, which is the function-word density whatlang needs and is
language-independent, since German capitalises nouns but still connects them
with lowercase articles and verbs. Measured after: drift is caught under all
three headings, and a keyword-shaped section no longer fires.

project_link_issues widened its generated side to every Projects section but
left the source side on the first, so a resume with both PROJECTS and SIDE
PROJECTS accused the user of inventing their own link - unclearably, since
repair routes the finding to the first Projects section. Both sides are now
symmetric.

cross_section_regression could revert a round that fixed every Critical because
one Warning appeared. It is now gated on the Critical count not improving. My
commissioning argument for the delta was wrong: I claimed the measured false
positives were carried rather than introduced, and round_is_worse's own doc
records the measurement as zero to four.

The splice gate had no test. Both guard tests rebuilt is_usable_replacement and
matches_requested_kind inside their own closure, so deleting a clause from
production left all 137 green while a docstring claimed the mutation was
verified. Extracted sections::accepts, called by production and tests alike.

Also: section_count counted heading LINES, so an ALL-CAPS employer inside a
single-section reply read as a second section and the regenerate button
silently no-opped; and representative_bullet could anchor a section on its own
heading.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): resolve the confirmation review, and fix the skills section shape

The previous commit fixed one review round and introduced regressions doing
so. Every finding below was measured before being fixed.

Removing the SectionKind allowlist put Skills sections in scope for the first
time, and looks_like_prose reads a canonically-lowercase tool list as prose -
the real casing of pandas, numpy, pytest, git, nginx and kubectl IS lowercase,
and the bar was one word in five. Measured against the pinned whatlang on a
German resume's own KENNTNISSE section: a false Critical, report.ok false, and
the repair loop burning calls on a correct section. The guard test for exactly
this passed only because its fixture happened to be Title-Case. The Skills
exclusion is back, ahead of looks_like_prose, which still covers the
list-shaped Experience case it was added for.

real_section_count made the incomplete classifier the sole arbiter of "is this
a second section", contradicting the same commit's other finding. certifications,
awards, languages, publications and work history are all in the parser's
SECTION_NAMES but absent from classify_section, so a reply naming them passed
the gate and was spliced whole - the doubling corruption, reopened. A heading
now counts when classify_section knows it OR the parser does.

looks_like_prose skipped every caseless script, because char::is_lowercase is
false throughout Arabic, Hebrew, CJK, Thai and Devanagari. Measured: an Arabic
Experience section at 148 significant chars was never checked, where it fired
before. It now decides per word, so an uncased word counts toward prose - the
whole-text form fails once the English heading is included in the checked text.

The Critical gate had removed the only signal that ever saw a doubling round.
duplicate.bullet is ungated again; only skill_not_demonstrated stays gated,
which matches the measurement that motivated the gate - every noise reading in
the doc names shared skill tokens, never duplicates.

Three behaviour changes had shipped with no test at all; validate/content/test.rs
was untouched. Five tests added and PROSE_LOWERCASE_WORD_RATIO pinned.

Separately, the skills section had no specified shape - resume_conventions.skills
is only the localised heading, so the model chose and the repo's own fixtures
disagree. It is now grouped inline lists, one line per group, with the bullet
form explicitly prohibited rather than merely undescribed: a bullet per skill
spends a line on one word, and an ATS extracts a comma list just as well.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): make an unroutable language finding a warning, and close three gate gaps

Seven review findings on the open pull request. Every one verified before being
fixed.

A language-drift Critical on a section the repair grammar cannot route was
unclearable. key_of maps SectionKind::Other to None, so a finding labelled
Volunteer, Awards, Certifications or Work History is dropped by
criticals_by_section: no repair runs, the regenerate button cannot reach it,
and the run parks at needsReview on a blocker nothing can lift. My own
prose-density change made it reachable by removing the kind allowlist, putting
every Other-kind section in scope for the first time. An audit of this branch
predicted this precise shape and I did not act on it.

It follows the rule this branch has applied throughout: a Critical whose remedy
cannot be executed is not a Critical. An unroutable section now warns. The
finding still reaches the quality report; it no longer blocks. Traded
deliberately: drift confined to such a section warns rather than blocks, which
is better than a block nobody can clear.

real_section_count missed ATX headings, so a reply using ## Leadership passed
the multi-section gate and was spliced whole - the doubling corruption, third
variant after the heading-line count and the classifier-only count. It now
reuses export::parser::strip_atx_heading rather than forking a second copy of
the shape test, since duplicated heuristics are a defect class this repo has
paid for before.

Unioning every generated Projects section made one invented URL report twice,
because the invention loop pushes per occurrence. New with the symmetry fix;
the existing test used distinct links so it could not see it. Deduped on the
canonical link.

context_anchor built the whole Summary and let fenced() truncate it silently;
it now caps where it is built. A guard test could pass through the identity
check rather than the heading count it targets, so the premise is pinned.

On the renderer side, resumeLanguage || jobAdLanguage picked the first
NON-EMPTY and validated only that, so an invalid legacy resumeLanguage
short-circuited a perfectly good jobAdLanguage and sent the run to detection.
Each field is now normalised and validated independently. Presence is not
validity - the same substitution behind every other defect on this branch.

fix(pipeline): catch per-section language drift, drop empty sections, and keep the regenerate language (#1003)

* fix(pipeline): catch per-section language drift, drop empty sections, keep the regenerate language

Three owner-reported defects, all downstream of one architectural change: PRs
#969 and #992 moved generation from ONE whole-document call to per-section
calls that cannot see their siblings. Before that, coherence was free.

Language drift. content.language_mismatch read the whole document, and
languages_align returns the DOMINANT language, so a majority vote hid exactly
the reported case. Measured: one Italian section in a long English resume went
undetected, two undetected, three detected. A per-section pass now runs when
the document-level read comes back clean.

It is scoped POSITIVELY to Summary/Experience/Projects rather than by excluding
Skills. Review caught why that matters: SectionKind has six variants and
classify_section has no heading list for Certifications, Awards, Publications
or Languages-spoken, so all of them land in Other. A correct English "AWS
Certified Solutions Architect (Professional, 2022)" block clears the character
floor and reads as non-English - an exclusion list silently admits every kind
nobody thought of. A false Critical here blanks keywordCoverage and suppresses
every alignment finding on the whole document, so the cost of over-reach is
higher than the miss.

Empty sections. My own #998 regression: "order the sections EXACTLY as … do
not drop" read as a manifest plus a ban on omitting anything, so the model
emitted Projects and Publications with nothing in them. The prompt now frames
the list as an order, not a checklist.

The guard is a Warning, not a Critical, and the severity is the design. repair
acts on Criticals and its remedy is to REGENERATE the section - asked to fill
an empty PROJECTS the model would invent projects, a fabrication in the one
part of this pipeline built to prevent them. Removal is the right remedy and
model::adapter::push_nonempty_section already does it structurally, so nothing
empty reaches the rendered document.

Regenerate language. useTailorPipeline re-detected from jobDesc every render
and treated "I could not tell" as "it is English", discarding a language the
run already knew. It now prefers the persisted value - normalized through
toLanguageCode first, because extractMetadata persists a display NAME
("German") while every other writer stores an ISO code and save_application
merges both into one record. Passing "German" through would have been worse
than the bug: normalize_language truncates it to "ge", which matches no
languages_align arm, turning the language checks off entirely for that
document.

head_commit.message:
fix(pipeline): catch per-section language drift, drop empty sections, and keep the regenerate language (#1003)

* fix(pipeline): catch per-section language drift, drop empty sections, keep the regenerate language

Three owner-reported defects, all downstream of one architectural change: PRs
#969 and #992 moved generation from ONE whole-document call to per-section
calls that cannot see their siblings. Before that, coherence was free.

Language drift. content.language_mismatch read the whole document, and
languages_align returns the DOMINANT language, so a majority vote hid exactly
the reported case. Measured: one Italian section in a long English resume went
undetected, two undetected, three detected. A per-section pass now runs when
the document-level read comes back clean.

It is scoped POSITIVELY to Summary/Experience/Projects rather than by excluding
Skills. Review caught why that matters: SectionKind has six variants and
classify_section has no heading list for Certifications, Awards, Publications
or Languages-spoken, so all of them land in Other. A correct English "AWS
Certified Solutions Architect (Professional, 2022)" block clears the character
floor and reads as non-English - an exclusion list silently admits every kind
nobody thought of. A false Critical here blanks keywordCoverage and suppresses
every alignment finding on the whole document, so the cost of over-reach is
higher than the miss.

Empty sections. My own #998 regression: "order the sections EXACTLY as … do
not drop" read as a manifest plus a ban on omitting anything, so the model
emitted Projects and Publications with nothing in them. The prompt now frames
the list as an order, not a checklist.

The guard is a Warning, not a Critical, and the severity is the design. repair
acts on Criticals and its remedy is to REGENERATE the section - asked to fill
an empty PROJECTS the model would invent projects, a fabrication in the one
part of this pipeline built to prevent them. Removal is the right remedy and
model::adapter::push_nonempty_section already does it structurally, so nothing
empty reaches the rendered document.

Regenerate language. useTailorPipeline re-detected from jobDesc every render
and treated "I could not tell" as "it is English", discarding a language the
run already knew. It now prefers the persisted value - normalized through
toLanguageCode first, because extractMetadata persists a display NAME
("German") while every other writer stores an ISO code and save_application
merges both into one record. Passing "German" through would have been worse
than the bug: normalize_language truncates it to "ge", which matches no
languages_align arm, turning the language checks off entirely for that
document.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): make the splice boundary and the accept rule survive per-section generation

An audit measured what #969/#992 broke when generation moved from one
whole-document call to per-section calls that cannot see their siblings. Five
findings, one root cause each side of the same seam: the splice trusted the
model's reply, and the accept rule could not see the damage.

A repair round could silently delete a job. company_survives lowercased the
ENTIRE generated document and substring-searched for the employer, so a
Summary reading "…at Acme Payments and Globex Logistics" spared the deletion
of the whole Globex entry from EXPERIENCE. Measured: roles 2 to 1,
factual.dropped_role never fired, round accepted and persisted. Survival is now
tested against the generated EXPERIENCE section, all of its lines, so an
ordinary bullet reword still matches.

A reply containing the whole document was accepted and spliced over one
section. is_usable_replacement checked for a fence tag, a leading heading and
one body line, and nothing about how many sections came back. Measured: 6
sections to 10, and because reorder_sections is a stable sort, linearize merely
parked the duplicates adjacent - the exported PDF showed four sections twice.
Under mutation it compounded to 4x as the loop re-accepted round after round.

A reply for a DIFFERENT section was accepted. The target was resolved by
SectionKey and the reply spliced without re-classifying it, so asking for
SUMMARY and receiving SKILLS silently destroyed the summary and created a
second skills section, which the next round then could not find. The reply's
own heading is now re-classified and a mismatch is discarded - the right remedy
for a bad attempt is to drop it, not to raise a Critical that would ask the
model to regenerate again.

Analysis::section_of_kind returned only the FIRST section of a kind, so an
invented link in a second Projects section produced zero Criticals. The
Critical-severity consumer now reads every matching section; the two
Warning-severity consumers keep the cheaper lookup, since the residual risk
there costs a missed Warning rather than a missed Critical.

round_is_worse could only see Criticals and absences, while its sibling
humanize_is_worse also guarded coverage and voice - and repair runs FIRST,
makes up to eight blind per-section rewrites, and had the weaker rule. It now
reverts on a drop in roles_output, the one metric that saw the deleted job, and
shares humanize's coverage guard rather than duplicating it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(pipeline): let a section rewrite see the document it belongs to

Before #969/#992 a resume was generated by ONE model call, so language, voice
and tense coherence came free. The staged pipeline broke generation into
per-section calls that cannot see their siblings and replaced that implicit
guarantee with a prompt instruction - and instructions drift. Three
user-visible bugs followed, including a resume whose summary was English, work
experience Italian, and skills English again.

repair_user passed the source resume, the one section being rewritten, its
issues and an optional note. Nothing told the model what the rest of the
document looked like. It now also receives a compact anchor: the Summary,
which carries the register, and one representative Experience bullet, which
carries tense and voice - each excluded by SectionKind when it IS the section
being rewritten, so a rewrite never matches the text it is replacing.

An anchor rather than the whole document because this is charged up to
MAX_SECTIONS_PER_ROUND x max_repair_attempts = 8 times per run. Capped at
SIBLING_CONTEXT_CAP, roughly twice the measured worst case in this crate's own
fixtures and far below the whole-document cap humanize uses for its single
pass. The trade: drift confined to Skills or Education against the anchor is
not prevented, only detected.

This is model-generated text re-entering a prompt, so ADR-010 applies exactly
as it does to a scraped job ad. document_context is registered in
FENCE_TAG_PATTERNS and covered by the existing load-bearing forgery loop;
removing the registration lets a forged closing tag leak through, which the
test now proves.

The user's own regenerate-this-section button inherits all of it, since
resume_pipeline_regenerate_section calls the same function.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(pipeline): revert a repair round that introduces cross-section incoherence

An audit found the codebase's only two cross-section coherence checks -
duplicate.bullet and consistency.skill_not_demonstrated - are computed and then
thrown away. repair acts on Criticals only, humanize on voice.* only. Measured
consequences, both accepted and persisted: a round that doubled the whole
document produced 5 duplicate.bullet warnings at duplicateRatio 1.00 and
shipped; a round that deleted an employment entry produced 4
skill_not_demonstrated warnings and shipped.

The naive fix is to revert when those warnings are present, and it is wrong.
The same audit measured them false-positiving under per-section generation:
rewording two Experience bullets to drop the exact tokens - the ordinary
outcome of a rewrite that cannot see the Skills section - raises four warnings
on a truthful document. An absolute threshold would revert good rounds and
would need calibrating against noise.

So the term is a DELTA, not a count. The question is not whether the document
carries cross-section warnings but whether THIS ROUND introduced any that were
not there before. Four before and four after reverts nothing; four before and
nine after reverts. That needs no threshold, is immune to the measured baseline
false positives, and matches the before/after shape round_is_worse already uses
for its newly-introduced-absence term.

Per code rather than summed, so a round that fixes two duplicate.bullet
warnings while introducing two skill_not_demonstrated ones cannot hide a
regression behind an unrelated improvement - a case a summed total reads as
flat, and which the mutation check confirmed only the per-code form catches.

Also closes two advisories from the security review of da4926f0: the anchor is
trimmed once at its source, so repair_system's gate and repair_user's own
emptiness test can no longer disagree about whether a document_context block
exists; and the context rule now says to match the language and tense OBSERVED
there, naming it a writing sample rather than asking the model to conform to
untrusted content.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(validate): do not read an unrecognised experience heading as deleted jobs

Security review found a HIGH regression introduced by this branch's own
scoping of the dropped-role survival search.

company_survives used to read the whole generated document, which let a
Summary sentence naming a former employer mask the deletion of that employer's
entire entry. Scoping the search to SectionKind::Experience closed that, but
turned a second fact into the same verdict: when the generated resume has NO
Experience-kind section, the scoped haystack is empty, so every source role
reads as deleted.

classify_section knows work experience, berufserfahrung, employment and a few
more - it does not know Work History or Selected Roles, which land in Other.
Measured on a resume carrying both roles verbatim: heading WORK EXPERIENCE
gives 0 issues, WORK HISTORY gives 2 factual.dropped_role Criticals, SELECTED
ROLES the same. Those are terminal, not merely wrong: criticals_by_section
routes them to SectionKey::Experience, find cannot locate it, no repair runs,
and the run parks at needsReview telling the user two jobs vanished from a
document that still lists them.

Reachability rose in this same branch, which is what makes it urgent rather
than theoretical: draft_system was loosened from "do not reorder, drop, or
invent" to "an ORDER, not a checklist" so the model is freer to choose its own
heading, and matches_requested_kind constrains only a repair reply, never the
draft.

Absent is not deleted. The search now falls back to the whole document when no
Experience-kind section exists, mirroring the guard project_link_issues
already had - preferring a possible miss over a guaranteed false Critical,
since the scoping exists to catch a rare regression and must not manufacture a
common one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): resolve the blocking findings from the pre-merge review ensemble

Three reviewer passes plus a security gate, run over the whole branch. Every
finding below was reproduced before being fixed.

The Rust suite was RED and I reported it green. cargo test --lib and
--test architecture do not build tests/eval.rs; CI's nextest --all-features
does. The corpus guard was doing exactly its job - the new Italian-drift
fixture was graded by nothing - and the command I ran was narrow enough to
miss it. The fixture is now registered in CASES.

generated_experience_lower fell back on TEXT emptiness rather than section
absence. A wiped Experience section still yields one blank line, so the joined
text is empty, the fallback fires, and an employer named in the Summary masks
the loss. Measured: a resume with its entire employment history deleted
reported factual.dropped_role = 0 and ok = true. It now tests section
existence, mirroring project_link_issues' own presence guard.

section_language_issues gated on a SectionKind allowlist, a proxy for "is this
prose" that was wrong in both directions - too narrow to see an Experience
section headed Work History, too wide for a keyword-shaped one that whatlang
misreads. Replaced with a prose-density test: the share of words opening
lowercase, which is the function-word density whatlang needs and is
language-independent, since German capitalises nouns but still connects them
with lowercase articles and verbs. Measured after: drift is caught under all
three headings, and a keyword-shaped section no longer fires.

project_link_issues widened its generated side to every Projects section but
left the source side on the first, so a resume with both PROJECTS and SIDE
PROJECTS accused the user of inventing their own link - unclearably, since
repair routes the finding to the first Projects section. Both sides are now
symmetric.

cross_section_regression could revert a round that fixed every Critical because
one Warning appeared. It is now gated on the Critical count not improving. My
commissioning argument for the delta was wrong: I claimed the measured false
positives were carried rather than introduced, and round_is_worse's own doc
records the measurement as zero to four.

The splice gate had no test. Both guard tests rebuilt is_usable_replacement and
matches_requested_kind inside their own closure, so deleting a clause from
production left all 137 green while a docstring claimed the mutation was
verified. Extracted sections::accepts, called by production and tests alike.

Also: section_count counted heading LINES, so an ALL-CAPS employer inside a
single-section reply read as a second section and the regenerate button
silently no-opped; and representative_bullet could anchor a section on its own
heading.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): resolve the confirmation review, and fix the skills section shape

The previous commit fixed one review round and introduced regressions doing
so. Every finding below was measured before being fixed.

Removing the SectionKind allowlist put Skills sections in scope for the first
time, and looks_like_prose reads a canonically-lowercase tool list as prose -
the real casing of pandas, numpy, pytest, git, nginx and kubectl IS lowercase,
and the bar was one word in five. Measured against the pinned whatlang on a
German resume's own KENNTNISSE section: a false Critical, report.ok false, and
the repair loop burning calls on a correct section. The guard test for exactly
this passed only because its fixture happened to be Title-Case. The Skills
exclusion is back, ahead of looks_like_prose, which still covers the
list-shaped Experience case it was added for.

real_section_count made the incomplete classifier the sole arbiter of "is this
a second section", contradicting the same commit's other finding. certifications,
awards, languages, publications and work history are all in the parser's
SECTION_NAMES but absent from classify_section, so a reply naming them passed
the gate and was spliced whole - the doubling corruption, reopened. A heading
now counts when classify_section knows it OR the parser does.

looks_like_prose skipped every caseless script, because char::is_lowercase is
false throughout Arabic, Hebrew, CJK, Thai and Devanagari. Measured: an Arabic
Experience section at 148 significant chars was never checked, where it fired
before. It now decides per word, so an uncased word counts toward prose - the
whole-text form fails once the English heading is included in the checked text.

The Critical gate had removed the only signal that ever saw a doubling round.
duplicate.bullet is ungated again; only skill_not_demonstrated stays gated,
which matches the measurement that motivated the gate - every noise reading in
the doc names shared skill tokens, never duplicates.

Three behaviour changes had shipped with no test at all; validate/content/test.rs
was untouched. Five tests added and PROSE_LOWERCASE_WORD_RATIO pinned.

Separately, the skills section had no specified shape - resume_conventions.skills
is only the localised heading, so the model chose and the repo's own fixtures
disagree. It is now grouped inline lists, one line per group, with the bullet
form explicitly prohibited rather than merely undescribed: a bullet per skill
spends a line on one word, and an ATS extracts a comma list just as well.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): make an unroutable language finding a warning, and close three gate gaps

Seven review findings on the open pull request. Every one verified before being
fixed.

A language-drift Critical on a section the repair grammar cannot route was
unclearable. key_of maps SectionKind::Other to None, so a finding labelled
Volunteer, Awards, Certifications or Work History is dropped by
criticals_by_section: no repair runs, the regenerate button cannot reach it,
and the run parks at needsReview on a blocker nothing can lift. My own
prose-density change made it reachable by removing the kind allowlist, putting
every Other-kind section in scope for the first time. An audit of this branch
predicted this precise shape and I did not act on it.

It follows the rule this branch has applied throughout: a Critical whose remedy
cannot be executed is not a Critical. An unroutable section now warns. The
finding still reaches the quality report; it no longer blocks. Traded
deliberately: drift confined to such a section warns rather than blocks, which
is better than a block nobody can clear.

real_section_count missed ATX headings, so a reply using ## Leadership passed
the multi-section gate and was spliced whole - the doubling corruption, third
variant after the heading-line count and the classifier-only count. It now
reuses export::parser::strip_atx_heading rather than forking a second copy of
the shape test, since duplicated heuristics are a defect class this repo has
paid for before.

Unioning every generated Projects section made one invented URL report twice,
because the invention loop pushes per occurrence. New with the symmetry fix;
the existing test used distinct links so it could not see it. Deduped on the
canonical link.

context_anchor built the whole Summary and let fenced() truncate it silently;
it now caps where it is built. A guard test could pass through the identity
check rather than the heading count it targets, so the premise is pinned.

On the renderer side, resumeLanguage || jobAdLanguage picked the first
NON-EMPTY and validated only that, so an invalid legacy resumeLanguage
short-circuited a perfectly good jobAdLanguage and sent the run to detection.
Each field is now normalised and validated independently. Presence is not
validity - the same substitution behind every other defect on this branch.

head_commit.message:
feat(scraping): treat an implausible scraped company name as absent (#1001)

* feat(scraping): treat an implausible scraped company name as absent

PR #960 shipped six cover letters carrying garbage company names - the
scraper returned things like "Apply now | LinkedIn" as the employer. Every
existing guard passed, and correctly: validate/content/factual.rs checks
generated text AGAINST the job ad, so reproducing a garbage company faithfully
is not a factual error. Nothing checked whether the ingested posting was sane
in the first place.

Adds is_implausible_company to scraping::trust - CTA debris, board names
standing in for an employer, separator and HTML wreckage, placeholders, and
implausible shapes - plus a TrustFlag::ImplausibleCompany raised by
assess_trust. That module's contract is flag-only, enrich never drop, so it
gains signal and blocks nothing.

Acting on it happens at two real boundaries rather than by blocking: the
pipeline blanks an implausible company before it can seed company research or
the persisted record, and export's filename falls back to the same default an
absent name already gets. Passing None rather than garbage means the existing
prompt contract takes over - it already says to name only the role when no
company is provided - so no prompt text changed.

The predicate is deliberately conservative: a false positive silently deletes
a real employer from a letter, which is worse than the bug. Johnson & Johnson,
Ben & Jerry's, Yahoo!, Booking.com and 37signals are pinned as accepted. A
bare single character is rejected, which does reject X - at that length the
overwhelming cause is scraper truncation, and the cost of being wrong is soft
because the letter simply names the role instead.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(scraping): stop the sanity gate rejecting real employers, and surface its flag

Review caught the failure mode that matters more than the bug: the predicate
deleted real companies. Confirmed by running it - Monster Worldwide, Xing SE,
Indeed Inc, Glassdoor Inc and Apply On Demand Inc were all judged implausible.
Every one hires directly and posts under its own name, so a letter would have
silently dropped a real employer.

Both offending rules matched too loosely. JOB_BOARD_NAMES rejected any name
CONTAINING a board token as a word; CTA_PHRASES substring-matched, which is
what caught "Apply On Demand Inc" via "apply on ". Both now match only when
the entire normalized name IS the board name or CTA phrase, so a bare
"LinkedIn" is still garbage while "Xing SE" is not. The originally reported
"Apply now | LinkedIn" is still rejected - by the separator rule, not by
either loosened list, and a test pins that so the coverage is not accidental.
"Apply on Indeed" becomes an accepted false negative, pinned as a deliberate
choice rather than left to be rediscovered as a regression.

The new TrustFlag variant never reached the frontend. It serializes as
implausibleCompany but the hand-maintained TS union and both locale files
still listed four flags, and TrustBadge calls t() unconditionally - so the
badge would have rendered the literal key on exactly the postings this branch
exists to fix, in both languages. Adds the union member and both strings.

The repo's purpose-built i18n key-drift guard stayed green through all of
that, because its fixture list derives from the same stale union it guards. A
guard sourced from the thing it guards is not a guard. Fixed structurally: an
exhaustive Record<TrustFlag, string> now lives in production code, so a
missing variant fails typecheck for the whole app rather than one test file.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(scraping): scope the company validator to the crate and bound its scan

Review findings on #1001, both correct.

is_implausible_company was pub with no out-of-crate caller - every use is
crate::scraping::trust::is_implausible_company from resume_pipeline and
export. Narrowed to pub(crate).

It also collected every char of the trimmed name before the length check
rejected anything over MAX_COMPANY_CHARS, so an arbitrarily long scraped value
allocated proportional to its full size. A scraped company field is untrusted,
arbitrary-length input, so bound the collect at MAX + 1 - the only length
question asked is "> MAX?", which MAX + 1 answers, and the char-ratio checks
further down run only on names that already passed that gate, where the cap is
a no-op.

Mutation-checked that the length rule is still genuinely reachable after the
change rather than assuming it: disabling it turns the absurdly-long fixture
red.

head_commit.message:
docs: fold the second adr tree into the knowledge base (#1000)

* docs: fold the second adr tree into the knowledge base

The repo had two ADR directories with colliding numbers: docs/adr/0013 was
email watching while adr-013 was the resume builder, and both got cited as
"ADR-13". It already caused a wrong citation.

docs/knowledge/decision-records/ is the canonical one - created 2026-05-31
with the knowledge base, indexed in its README, owned by project-steward, and
the only one the docs-standards skill points at. docs/adr/ appeared twelve
days later, carried no index and no owner, and grew to 23 records because
nothing stopped it.

The files are moved but deliberately NOT renumbered. An ADR is a dated record
and its number is cited from commit messages, merged PR bodies, code comments
and the published tech radar; the landing benchmark and metrics snapshots are
generated captures of commit text that must not be rewritten. Renumbering
would falsify all of it, so the series is folded in as-is and marked closed -
new ADRs continue the adr-NNN sequence.

Every reference follows: 24 live files, the tech radar's ADR_DIR and its
public GitHub blob links, and the relative links inside the moved files, which
gained a directory level. Generated landing snapshots under public/ are left
untouched as the historical records they are. check:tech-radar,
check:agent-system and check:landing-drift all pass, and the knowledge README
now indexes all 57 ADRs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test: repoint the tech-radar fixture at the unified adr directory

check-tech-radar.test.mjs builds a synthetic repo and writes its fixture ADR
to docs/adr/, which no longer exists after the trees were folded together, so
the real-adrSlug case resolved against nothing and the check exited 1 where the
test expected 0.

The test was right to fail - it is asserting that a valid slug resolves, and
the directory it resolves against moved. Fixture repointed at
docs/knowledge/decision-records/; the assertions are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: correct accuracy drift the adr move surfaced

Moving 23 ADRs made git read them as new files, so review examined content
nobody had re-read since it was written. Ten inaccuracies came back, none
introduced by the move. Kept separate from the move commit so those 2211
relocated lines stay verifiable as byte-identical.

Two mattered. ADR-0005's privacy guarantee allowed egress only for services
the user configures or invokes plus crash reports, while its own body
documents an on-launch updater check - README.md already discloses that, so
the ADR was the wrong one; the guarantee now names both classes of automatic
app-initiated egress. ADR-0009 still described profile.get as authenticated by
a per-frame pairing token, a contract ADR-0010 retired in favour of the mutual
HMAC handshake, so anyone reading it would have implemented the wrong auth
model; it now points at ADR-0010.

The rest: ADR-0005 counted seven egress classes where it lists eight; ADR-0008's
title claimed three surfaces where its body describes four and conflated the
removed pre-push LLM lane with the deterministic pre-push gates that remain;
ADR-0011 used a field name the bridge does not have and presented snapshot
symbols ADR-0012 superseded as current; ADR-0013 claimed email content never
leaves the device, which conflated IMAP ingress with egress; ADR-0019
prescribed a prohibited cat command and overstated portability for a file that
is now ESM-only; ADR-0022 opened two lines with #936 and #937, which Markdown
parses as malformed headings.

Decisions and rationale are untouched - only claims that no longer match the
code.

head_commit.message:
fix(export): restore lost bold, kill the letter placeholder, and make section order deterministic (#998)

* fix(export): never promote a template placeholder to the letter signature title

Every German cover letter rendered an unfilled template slot as the candidate
job title: "Ihr Name" appeared under the signature, after the sign-off.

The model reproduces a letter template placeholder verbatim; parse_cover_letter
then applies its post-signoff rule (first non-blank non-name line becomes
signature_title) and renders it. complete_letter_text does not intervene:
its idempotency guard sees the model-emitted salutation and sign-off, so it
returns the text unchanged.

This is the drift ADR-034 Consequence #2 records as unguarded - the existing
check fires when the prompt sentence changes, not when the output shape does.

Adds one shared predicate, locale::letter::is_template_placeholder, covering
whole-line slot syntax and the known en/de literal tokens. The parser skips
such a line instead of promoting it, and validate/content/letter.rs raises the
new Critical letter.template_placeholder so a placeholder cannot reach export
silently again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(resume): resolve section order from the market instead of letting the model pick

The résumé's section order was an LLM free choice, re-rolled on every
generation. ResumeStrategy.section_order was a free-form Vec<String> whose
schema was {"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}} - no enum, no market
awareness - and the draft was told only, in prose, to "follow its section
order". No Rust code ever read the field.

Meanwhile the ATS-correct ordering lived in a market-blind ATS_ORDER const
that linearize() applied only in ATS mode, so it never governed the normal
render path.

Adds locale::resume::section_order_for(market) as the single order source:
the default (skills-driven US/UK) order puts Skills above Experience as an
early keyword block, while DE follows Lebenslauf convention with skills late.
Both the draft prompt and linearize() read that one function, so the model's
order and the exporter's order cannot disagree, and section_order is removed
from ResumeStrategy entirely.

Market (the request's locale) is threaded separately from lang (the written
language): a candidate can write an English résumé for a German posting.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(export): close two holes the critic found in the placeholder and order guards

Both guards passed their tests while leaving the defect class open.

Bracket placeholders were unprotected. parse_cover_letter checks the line
AFTER strip_md_links, which unwraps any whole [...] span because it cannot
tell a template slot from a markdown link label. So "[Job Title]" arrived at
the predicate as "Job Title" and was promoted to signature_title. The bracket
branch was dead at the only call site that stops bad output; the original
"[Your Title]" test passed only because it collapses to a literal already in
PLACEHOLDER_TOKENS. Now the raw line is tested as well as the stripped one,
with [Job Title] and [Position] pinned as regressions.

Two market-id namespaces reach section_order_for and they disagree.
LocaleProfile collapses DE/AT/CH into the id "dach", recommend::pick_locale
returns it, and the AI-Generate résumé export path forwards it verbatim -
only the cover-letter arm normalizes. Matching just "de" gave those users the
default US order, contradicting the whole point of the change. Now accepts the
same alias set LocaleProfile::get already uses.

Also corrects the ADR-034 update, which claimed letter.template_placeholder
fails the export's content validation. It does not: validate::content is never
called from export/, so the Critical is a generation-time report entry and the
parser is what actually stops the bytes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(resume): keep the default section order reverse-chronological

Owner call after review: Experience leads, Skills follows. Skills-above-
Experience is real advice, but for career-changers and entry-level candidates
- on the continuous-history résumé this app mostly serves it reads as
compensating for thin experience, and it departs from the reverse-
chronological baseline resume-export-standards anchors on. Section position
does not affect ATS extraction either way, since parsers bucket by heading
text, so this is a convention call rather than a parsing one.

DE_ORDER is unchanged. The point of the change stands: the order is now
deterministic, market-aware, and shared with the draft prompt, rather than an
LLM free choice re-rolled every generation.

Both markets now lead with Experience, so the tests that proved market
awareness by comparing Skills-vs-Experience no longer discriminated - one
asserted two identical strings differed. Re-anchored them on Skills-vs-
Education, which is where the two orders actually diverge, and re-ran the
mutation check: pointing the German arm at DEFAULT_ORDER fails six tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: correct a section-order comment left stale by the default revert

The Aria ATS reading-order test still described "us" as the skills-driven
order after the default reverted to reverse-chronological.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: explain what the license means for contributors

CONTRIBUTING.md said nothing about licensing, so a prospective contributor
had no way to tell what rights they were granting by opening a PR - which is
the actual friction, more than the license terms themselves.

Adds a Licensing and Contributions section: what PolyForm Noncommercial
permits (use, fork, modify, internal company use, research, PRs) versus what
it does not (resale, paid SaaS, competing products), that contributors keep
copyright in their own work since there is no CLA, that authorship is
preserved, and that pre-2026-06-14 MIT-era contributions were not
retroactively relicensed. Also asks anyone actually blocked by a term to say
so in an issue rather than leaving quietly.

No change to the license itself.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(export): give entry subtitles and header contact lines real breathing room

Three rendering defects, all fixed centrally rather than per template.

The entry subtitle sat 1pt under its title, so the role was crammed against
the company and the degree against the university. sp-subtitle-gap is shared
by eleven resume templates, so raising it to 3pt fixes all of them at once.

The name-to-contact gap was hardcoded in eight templates at six different
values (3, 4, 5, 6, 9pt) while _scale.typ already defined sp-name-below = 9pt
for exactly that purpose and nobody used it. All of them now route through
the token, resume and cover-letter templates alike.

Education entry titles rendered at regular weight everywhere except the
Academic template, because emphasize_education was t.id == TemplateId::Academic.
The university now renders bold like the company. This also closes a real
PDF/DOCX divergence: RunOpts::entry_title already forced bold unconditionally,
so DOCX had been bolding education all along while PDF had not, contradicting
the golden-parity claim in adr-002.

Raising the Awesome gap pushed a title-plus-long-contact header past the 28mm
band floor (measured 81.79pt vs 79.37pt), so band-min-h's has-title branch
moves to 29mm.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(export): restore bold in resume bullets and regroup the letter signature

Bold never rendered in a resume bullet, in any template, in either backend.
parse_line strips markdown into `clean` up front, and the bullet arm matched
BULLET_RE against `clean` rather than `trimmed`, so the captured text had
already lost its `**` markers before tokenize_rich ever saw it - it emitted
bold: false every time. The two-space-gap JobEntry arm had the same defect,
and the adapter's JobEntry arm compounded it by tokenizing line.text
(stripped) instead of line.raw. Every other parse_line arm was already
correct; audited all of them.

This mattered beyond looks: generation deliberately emphasises keywords with
`**`, and every tailored resume was silently losing that emphasis on the way
to the page.

A markdown link whose label is just the bare URL now renders through
url_label, so a contact reads "LinkedIn" rather than the full href as body
text. Contact links themselves already survived - that half of the reported
symptom had a different cause than assumed.

Entry subtitles were still crammed at 3pt, so sp-subtitle-gap goes to 6pt
(measured 10.56 -> 13.56pt on SwissMinimal).

Cover-letter sign-off, name and role are now one unbreakable block across all
six layouts, driven by two shared tokens instead of six per-layout literals,
so a page break can no longer separate a name from its sign-off. letter_refined
and letter_sidebar stack contact entries vertically: a long contact line was
claiming enough of the header grid's auto column to wrap the candidate's name
onto two lines.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(export): unstick the header role from the name in meridian and awesome

The name-to-role gap was the last hardcoded header spacing literal. Only
meridian.typ and awesome.typ set an explicit `above:` on the title block, both
at 2pt, so the role sat flush against the name while every other template
omits the value and inherits sane spacing. Both now use sp-subtitle-gap, the
same token letter_refined's header role gap already uses - it is the same
title-to-subtitle relationship.

Awesome's band is content-measured, so the taller gap overflowed the has-title
floor again exactly as it did when sp-name-below landed: 85.79pt against the
82.20pt (29mm) floor. band-min-h's has-title branch moves 29mm -> 31mm and the
pinned expectation in awesome_band_contains_its_white_header_text moves with
it. That constant has now been bumped twice by header-gap changes, so its doc
comment says so and names the test that catches it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(export): address review findings on the export and licensing changes

A lookalike host could wear a trusted brand label. url_label matched known
domains with host.starts_with, so https://linkedin.com.evil.example rendered
as "LinkedIn" while pointing elsewhere - a deceptive link in an exported
document. The helper predates this branch, but routing markdown links through
it made the path reachable. Now matches exactly or on a dot boundary, for all
ten domains, against the path-stripped host.

The licensing table in CONTRIBUTING.md was wrong in both directions. LICENSE
grants any noncommercial purpose, personal use without anticipated commercial
application, and use by charities, schools, public research and government. It
does NOT grant internal use at a for-profit company, which the table claimed.
And PolyForm Noncommercial carries no non-compete clause, so a noncommercial
derivative is permitted, which the table denied. The boundary is commercial
versus noncommercial and nothing else; LICENSE is now named as authoritative.

A golden test passed with bold disabled entirely. Comparing the two entry-title
widths to each other proves only that they agree, so un-bolding both kept it
green - precisely the regression it exists to catch. It is now anchored to a
known-regular reference rendering the same string. Every other assertion added
on this branch was checked for the same self-referential shape; none share it.

Also: is_template_placeholder is exposed from the locale module root rather
than a leaf; the 26pt signature gap is emitted only when a sign-off actually
rendered, across all six letter layouts; market ids are canonicalised through
LocaleProfile::get before linearize, so de-DE and de_AT reach DE_ORDER; the
resume paths default to "intl" like the letter paths instead of the language
tag "en"; and is_bare_url_label lowercases before stripping a prefix so
HTTPS:// and WWW. no longer defeat it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

versus noncommercial and nothing else; LICENSE is now named as authoritative.
